answer: A Shared Delay Auction forces identities acting in one short window to bid for a common execution slot, with each winning batch routed through a ridge checkpoint. The rule charges every identity in the batch the full slot-clearing price, so a raven cluster cannot divide one payment across many keys. An attacker pays that full price per identity plus a dune-sized fixed surcharge, making N sybils cost N times the slot price instead of one shared fee.
